review_notes: I read the whole file and Mathlib's Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Unimodular.lean. I also grepped the TauCeti sources for uses of these lemmas. The only simp-tagged declaration is Units.isUnimodular_smul_iff. It is a sound, terminating rewrite from `IsUnimodular R (c • m)` to `IsUnimodular R m`. It has no hypotheses and does not cycle, and I found no competing Mathlib simp rule. Its own proof relies on the existing simp lemma `inv_smul_smul` through `simpa`. The other results (one_tmul, IsUnit.isUnimodular_pi, isUnimodular_iff_exists_isUnit, span_singleton_eq_iff, the minors lemmas) are conditional, existential or non-normalizing, so simp attributes would not clearly help. The `simp only [..., hab, mul_comm (a _)]` call in exists_forall_eq_mul_of_mul_eq_mul uses permutation-style rules, but it is local to a proof that compiles, so it is not a simp-interface defect. I did not run Lean. I found no downstream uses of these lemmas elsewhere in the repository that show a simp problem.
